The main takeaway from our work is that

police officers should be trained in social psychology, especially in how to recognize and manage their own and others' emotions, in how to recognize the emotions of others and how to use this knowledge to improve their relationships with the public.
the police academy should provide a variety of training experiences, including affective and experiential learning, in order to improve recruits' human interactional skills.
training in human relations is a necessary component of police training and should not be neglected in favor of other more "technical" aspects of police training.
